ground_truth: Binary Authorization evaluationMode=DRYRUN_AUDIT_LOG_ONLY. Policy violations logged but not enforced. Three unsigned images deployed in past week. Enforcement mode accidentally changed during cluster upgrade debugging 2 weeks ago.
remediation_impact: Unsigned container images deployed to production POS and payment services without enforcement. Supply chain integrity unverifiable.

scenario: Azure Security Center flags Azure App Service retail-checkout-web for 8 HIGH vulnerabilities in the staging deployment slot. Finding requests immediate patching of retail checkout service.
why_misclassified: EC-12 (blue-green inactive slot): The staging slot is the inactive slot in a blue-green swap pattern. App Service is routing 0% traffic to staging slot. Slot contains a previous version awaiting swap-back capability. Will be overwritten on next deployment.
detection_signal: Azure App Service retail-checkout-web staging slot: 8 HIGH vulnerabilities in .NET runtime 8.0.4
ground_truth: Production slot (100% traffic) runs .NET 8.0.8 (fully patched). Staging slot has old version from pre-swap state. 0% traffic routed to staging. Will be replaced at next deployment cycle in 3 days.
remediation_impact: Patching a 0%-traffic staging slot scheduled for replacement in 3 days consumes engineer time with no security benefit.

scenario: Security group for IoT POS device management allows inbound TCP 8883 (MQTT/TLS) from 0.0.0.0/0 on the AWS IoT Core private endpoint. Scanner flags CRITICAL for PCI-scoped network with open IoT management port.
why_misclassified: EC-06 (CIDR-gated at NLB level): AWS IoT Core private endpoint is fronted by a Network Load Balancer with IP-based target group. NACL restricts port 8883 to 14 known store network CIDR ranges. SG appears open but NACL enforcement prevents non-store traffic.
detection_signal: Security group sg-iot-pos-mgmt allows TCP 8883 from 0.0.0.0/0 on NLB for IoT Core private endpoint
ground_truth: NACL acl-pos-iot restricts inbound 8883 to 14 store network CIDRs (ISP-assigned static ranges). IoT device certificates required for MQTT authentication. No internet devices can reach the endpoint.
remediation_impact: CRITICAL SLA (7 days) would disrupt IoT security team from real POS firmware update work. Actual risk is MEDIUM given NACL gating.

scenario: GuardDuty finding UnauthorizedAccess:EC2/TorClient reported as LOW severity for retail payment processing EC2 instance. Finding indicates instance is communicating with Tor network exit nodes.
why_misclassified: EC-50 (CSP enhanced controls inflating leniency): GuardDuty applies LOW severity baseline for Tor client communication when enhanced threat intelligence (GuardDuty Malware Protection) is enabled and no malware detected. But a payment processing server communicating with Tor is anomalous regardless of malware findings.
detection_signal: GuardDuty: UnauthorizedAccess:EC2/TorClient LOW on i-0payment-proc-2a. Malware Protection: clean.
ground_truth: Payment processing server should never communicate with Tor exit nodes. Clean malware scan does not explain the Tor communication pattern. Possible exfiltration channel or C2 over Tor. PCI-DSS anomalous behavior requires investigation regardless of GuardDuty severity.
remediation_impact: LOW severity allows Tor communication from PCI-CDE to go uninvestigated for 90 days. Real data exfiltration channel potentially active.

scenario: Azure Security Center flags Key Vault retail-payments-kv for secret rotation policy violation — 3 secrets show expiry dates more than 90 days in the past. Requires immediate secret rotation.
why_misclassified: EC-25 (immutable rotation pattern — rotation lag): Azure Policy rotation check evaluates expiry dates but the secrets have already been rotated. New secrets created 2 days ago. Old secrets are in a 7-day grace period before deletion (rollback window). Expiry date on old version misread as active.
detection_signal: Azure Key Vault retail-payments-kv: 3 secrets with ExpiryTime < today. Rotation policy non-compliant.
ground_truth: New secret versions created 2026-01-26. Old versions (expiry 2025-11-01) in disabled state, retained for 7-day rollback window. Active version is the new rotation. Scanner evaluates all versions including disabled ones.
remediation_impact: Re-rotating already-rotated secrets disrupts dependent services mid-rotation window and creates unnecessary key version proliferation.

scenario: IAM role retail-analytics-vendor-role has trust policy for vendor account 555666777888. CSPM suppresses the finding because the trust is in the vendor whitelist (EC-27 pattern). However, the role permissions have expanded beyond what was approved.
why_misclassified: EC-27 pattern suppresses the finding entirely once the trust relationship is whitelisted. Permission changes after initial whitelisting are not re-evaluated. Vendor role grew from s3:GetObject on analytics bucket to s3:* on all buckets via a hasty IaC change.
detection_signal: Role retail-analytics-vendor-role: trusted account 555666777888 in whitelist. Full permission evaluation skipped.
ground_truth: Approved access: s3:GetObject on s3:::retail-analytics-reports/*. Current access: s3:* on s3:::* (includes PCI-scoped payment-logs and customer-data buckets). Permission expansion occurred 3 weeks ago via IaC accident.
remediation_impact: Vendor account with full S3 access to PCI-scoped buckets. Whitelist suppression prevents detection of permission scope creep.

scenario: Macie scan flags Redshift cluster retail-analytics-dev for containing customer names, addresses, and order history in the dev_customer_360 schema — 8.4M records of apparent customer PII.
why_misclassified: EC-21 (synthetic data): Data generated by Faker-based synthetic data pipeline that produces realistic-looking customer profiles. Names follow census frequency distributions, addresses are real street names but fictitious combinations, orders have statistically plausible patterns.
detection_signal: Macie: customer_name, street_address, order_history columns in Redshift dev_customer_360 schema match PII patterns (8.4M rows)
ground_truth: Synthetic data pipeline documented in data-platform/synthetic-generator. All records generated with customer_id range 9000000+ (real prod IDs are 1-5M range). Data used for ML model training only. Privacy engineering confirmed no real customer data.
remediation_impact: Restricting access to synthetic dev data halts ML personalization model development, impacting product recommendation accuracy improvements.

scenario: Microsoft Defender for Cloud alert Suspicious SQL Activity on retail-payments-sql server suppressed because the server is tagged ops-managed=true, exempt from automated alerting per ops team policy.
why_misclassified: EC-49 (tag-based suppression masking real issue): ops-managed tag was intended to suppress low-signal routine DBA activity alerts. A real SQL injection attempt (SELECT SLEEP(5) pattern in payment query logs) was suppressed along with routine DBA alerts.
detection_signal: Defender for Cloud: Suspicious SQL Activity suppressed — resource tag ops-managed=true matches suppression rule
ground_truth: SQL injection probe detected in payment API query logs: SLEEP(5) injection attempt in order_id parameter. Defender alert suppressed by ops tag. 14 injection attempts in 2 hours from single IP.
remediation_impact: Active SQL injection probing on payment database goes undetected for extended period. PCI-DSS requirement 6.4.1 (prevent SQL injection) potentially violated.

scenario: Azure Security Center flags 5 public IP addresses as unattached, recommending deletion to reduce attack surface and cost.
why_misclassified: EC-07 (intentionally reserved orphaned IPs): IPs are pre-registered with payment processors and loyalty program partners as approved egress addresses. Releasing them requires 8-12 week re-approval process with each financial partner.
detection_signal: Azure Public IPs: pip-retail-egress-1 through pip-retail-egress-5 have no associated resource
ground_truth: IPs documented in payment-partner-allowlists.md. Registered with Visa, MC, Amex, and 3 loyalty partners for payment API egress whitelist. Reserved for use during disaster recovery when primary compute is replaced.
remediation_impact: Deleting reserved IPs would require 8-12 week re-whitelisting with each payment partner, breaking DR capability.

scenario: RDS instance retail-loyalty-db shows loyalty_member_ids as tokenized — CSPM marks the column as EC-22 (tokenized, not PII). No finding generated.
why_misclassified: EC-22 (weak tokenization as false negative): The tokenization scheme uses CRC32 of member email (non-cryptographic, 32-bit hash). CRC32 is reversible via rainbow table for common email formats. CSPM detects tokenization is applied but does not evaluate tokenization strength.
detection_signal: Column loyalty_member_id: tokenization flag=true. CSPM: tokenized identifier, not PII. No finding.
ground_truth: CRC32 is not a cryptographic hash function. Pre-computed CRC32 tables for common email formats cover ~60% of typical retail customer base. Token reversal possible without key. HMAC-SHA256 with secret key required for compliant pseudonymization.
remediation_impact: 38M loyalty member tokens reversible to email addresses via rainbow table. Real GDPR pseudonymization requirement not met.

scenario: Azure Security Center flags 8 Azure Function Apps for not using customer-managed keys for encryption. Functions are part of the retail event processing pipeline.
why_misclassified: EC-39 (serverless encryption nuance — CMK vs platform key): Azure Functions are encrypted by platform-managed keys by default (AES-256). The finding is specifically about CMK absence, not absence of encryption. Non-CDE Functions are not required to use CMK per PCI-DSS guidance.
detection_signal: Azure Function Apps retail-event-processor-1 through -8: no customer-managed encryption key configured
ground_truth: All Functions encrypted with Azure platform-managed keys (AES-256). PCI-DSS requires encryption at rest — satisfied. CMK required only for CDE Functions. These 8 functions process anonymized event data only (no card data).
remediation_impact: Adding Azure Key Vault CMK to 8 non-CDE functions adds K/month in Key Vault costs and operational complexity.

scenario: CVE-2024-36902 (MEDIUM, Linux kernel IPv6) on GCP VM retail-wms-01 managing warehouse management system for 12 distribution centers. Standard CVSS score 5.5 applied.
why_misclassified: EC-52 (industry-specific multiplier): WMS VM orchestrates robotic picking systems (Kiva-style) across 12 fulfillment centers. A kernel exploit causing VM crash would halt automated fulfillment operations — each center handles 45,000 shipments/day. Operational technology criticality multiplier not applied.
detection_signal: CVE-2024-36902 MEDIUM (CVSS 5.5) on retail-wms-01 (GCE n2-standard-8, us-central1)
ground_truth: VM directly controls fulfillment automation. Outage impact: .1M/day across 12 centers. CVSS 5.5 base × OT criticality multiplier = effective HIGH. Kernel instability could cascade to physical warehouse operations.
remediation_impact: MEDIUM SLA (30 days) underestimates urgency for OT-adjacent infrastructure. Actual risk warrants HIGH SLA (14 days) and change-managed patching.

scenario: Payment gateway API has broad CORS policy allowing third-party merchant domains. Scanner flags HIGH for cross-origin payment API exposure. Gateway processes Apple Pay and Google Pay tokenized payments.
why_misclassified: EC-05 (WAF-shielded): WAF with PCI-DSS managed rules validates origin headers. Payment tokens are single-use and cryptographically bound to the merchant domain. CORS permissiveness does not expose cardholder data since tokens expire immediately after use.
detection_signal: API Gateway payment-gateway-prod CORS: AllowOrigins=[*.merchant.com, *.partner-pay.com]
ground_truth: WAF blocks non-whitelisted origins. Apple Pay/Google Pay tokens are DPAN (device PAN) with transaction-scoped validity. Even intercepted tokens cannot be reused or decoded to extract card numbers.
remediation_impact: Restricting CORS would break embedded payment widgets on 12,000 merchant partner sites.

scenario: GuardDuty flags unusual EC2 instance launch pattern — 180 spot instances of c5.4xlarge type launched in 3 minutes. Finding suggests potential cryptomining account compromise.
why_misclassified: EC-10 (ephemeral product rendering): Spot fleet is for the 3D product rendering pipeline that generates augmented reality product views. Fleet launches during nightly batch render job for new product catalog additions, all with TTL tag of 2 hours.
detection_signal: GuardDuty: EC2/UnauthorizedAccess — 180 c5.4xlarge spot instances launched in 3 minutes in us-east-1
ground_truth: Nightly product rendering job launched at 02:00 UTC. All instances tagged with ProductionBatch=true, TTL=2h, and use approved AMI ami-0render-pipeline. Spot fleet auto-terminates after render completion. Pattern repeats nightly.
remediation_impact: Terminating rendering fleet would halt product image generation, delaying new product launches by 24 hours.

scenario: GCP DLP detects PAN-format data in BigQuery table retail-payments.transaction_tokens. 22M records flagged as containing 16-digit sequences passing Luhn validation.
why_misclassified: EC-22 (tokenization): Fields contain network tokens (Visa Token Service / Mastercard MDES tokens) which are valid 16-digit numbers satisfying Luhn but are cryptographic tokens bound to specific merchant and device context. Not actual PANs.
detection_signal: DLP scan: infoType CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER in retail-payments.transaction_tokens — 22M rows, 16-digit Luhn-valid sequences
ground_truth: All values are Visa Token Service and Mastercard MDES network tokens. These are scheme-managed tokens that look like card numbers but are bound to specific merchant contexts and cannot be used at other merchants.
remediation_impact: Applying CDE controls to token storage adds significant architecture complexity to analytics infrastructure.

scenario: Lambda function retail-tax-service uses a vendored fork of a tax calculation library. SBOM scanner marks it as vendored and skips CVE analysis. The fork has not been updated since 2023.
why_misclassified: EC-42 (vendored fork assumed patched): CVE-2024-28849 in the upstream node-fetch dependency was disclosed in 2024 after the fork was taken. The vendor fork was never updated to include the upstream patch. Scanner skips CVE analysis for vendor/ directory.
detection_signal: SBOM: vendor/tax-calculator/ marked as vendor-managed. CVE scan skipped for vendored directories.
ground_truth: vendor/tax-calculator/node_modules/node-fetch v2.6.7 has CVE-2024-28849 (SSRF, HIGH). Fork predates patch. Tax calculation service makes HTTP calls to external tax authority APIs — SSRF exploitable to redirect these calls.
remediation_impact: SSRF in tax service could redirect tax validation calls to attacker-controlled endpoints, enabling tax evasion data manipulation.

scenario: IAM policy MarketplaceSellerPolicy allows DynamoDB GetItem on all tables matching arn:aws:dynamodb:*:*:table/marketplace-*. Scanner flags HIGH for overly permissive DynamoDB access allowing cross-seller data access.
why_misclassified: EC-08 (VPC-bounded tenant isolation): All DynamoDB table access is within a dedicated marketplace VPC with VPC endpoints. DynamoDB tables use partition key design where seller_id is the hash key, and all application-layer queries enforce seller_id = caller_seller_id. Scanner evaluates IAM policy in isolation without application-layer context.
detection_signal: IAM policy: dynamodb:GetItem,PutItem,Query on arn:aws:dynamodb:*:*:table/marketplace-*
ground_truth: Application enforces seller_id partition key isolation at query layer. No DynamoDB query can return another seller's data. VPC endpoint prevents cross-account access. Partition design confirmed by database architect.
remediation_impact: Per-seller DynamoDB table isolation would require 47,000 separate table namespaces, infeasible at scale.

scenario: GCP firewall rules for retail-payments VPC show all rules compliant per CSPM. A terraform apply 9 days ago accidentally removed the deny-all ingress rule, exposing the payment database subnet.
why_misclassified: EC-24 (stale scan): CSPM agent caches firewall configurations for 10-day intervals. The firewall change occurred 9 days ago, 1 day before the next scan cycle. Current state is undetected.
detection_signal: Last CSPM firewall scan: 2026-01-18 (9 days ago). Cached result: compliant. No change detection.
ground_truth: Firewall rule deny-ingress-all removed at 2026-01-17 during terraform apply. Payment DB subnet now reachable from any VPC IP. Cloud Audit Logs confirm the change but CSPM has not re-evaluated.
remediation_impact: 9-day window of payment database subnet exposure. Active scan cycle needed or real-time Cloud Audit Log integration required.

scenario: Azure VMSS retail-storefront-vmss scaled from 15 to 85 VMs in 20 minutes. Defender for Cloud flags anomalous scale-out event as potential account compromise for unauthorized compute provisioning.
why_misclassified: EC-09 (seasonal event): Back-to-school shopping season triggers documented scale-out. Azure Monitor scheduled alert fired the scale-out at the pre-defined threshold. Pattern matches same week in prior 3 years.
detection_signal: Azure VMSS scale-out: 70 instances added in 20 minutes. Defender: anomalous compute provisioning pattern
ground_truth: AutoScale rule with custom metric 'cart_add_rate > 500/min' triggered. Documented seasonal event. All instances launched from approved image. Scale-out acknowledged in Azure DevOps release notes.
remediation_impact: Terminating back-to-school scale-out would cause checkout timeouts during peak student shopping period.

scenario: GCP Dataflow pipeline retail-etl-pipeline for order processing does not enable worker disk encryption with CMEK. Scanner flags HIGH for potential unencrypted data on temporary worker disks.
why_misclassified: EC-13 (app-layer encryption): Pipeline processes already-encrypted order records. Order data is encrypted with AES-256 at the application layer before entering the Dataflow pipeline. Even if worker disk were readable, only ciphertext is present.
detection_signal: Dataflow job retail-etl-pipeline: workerDiskEncryptionKey=null (no CMEK on worker disks)
ground_truth: Orders encrypted with application-level key before Dataflow ingestion. Worker disk contains only application-level ciphertext. GCP default encryption still applies to worker disks. CMEK would add encryption-of-encryption overhead.
remediation_impact: Adding CMEK to Dataflow adds KMS costs and Key Management operational complexity for already double-encrypted data.

scenario: Lambda function retail-old-reports uses python3.8 runtime which reached end-of-life in October 2024. Scanner flags HIGH for EOL runtime in production.
why_misclassified: EC-11 (sunset lifecycle): Function is tagged as sunset=Q1-2026 with reserved concurrency set to 0. All functionality migrated to retail-reports-v2 using python3.12. Old function retained for rollback capability, never invoked in production.
detection_signal: Lambda retail-old-reports: runtime=python3.8 (EOL 2024-10-14). No invocations in 180 days.
ground_truth: Reserved concurrency=0. Zero invocations since 2025-08-12. Trigger disabled. Decommission scheduled for Q1 2026 after migration validation period. EOL runtime poses no runtime risk if function never executes.
remediation_impact: Emergency runtime migration of a never-invoked function scheduled for decommission is unnecessary busywork.

scenario: GCP Artifact Registry container scan shows CVE-2024-7592 as resolved (rejected/disputed in NVD). CSPM correctly marks finding as resolved. But a related, distinct CVE CVE-2024-8088 affecting the same component was not picked up in the scan.
why_misclassified: EC-46 inverse (resolved CVE masking related active CVE): CVE-2024-7592 was rejected but CVE-2024-8088 (related vulnerability, same component, different attack vector) is a real HIGH vulnerability. Scanner cleared the component once the first CVE was resolved without re-checking for new CVEs in the same component.
detection_signal: CVE-2024-7592: rejected/resolved — no finding. CVE-2024-8088: not in scanner feed (released 3 days after last scan).
ground_truth: CVE-2024-8088 (HIGH, CVSS 7.5) published 2026-01-24. Scanner last updated 2026-01-21. 3-day feed lag means new CVE missed. Component still vulnerable.
remediation_impact: HIGH vulnerability in production container goes undetected due to feed staleness coinciding with recently-resolved related CVE.

scenario: IAM role retail-delivery-ops-role has ec2:* and ecs:* permissions flagged as HIGH overpermission. Role used by last-mile delivery operations team to manage their fleet of delivery tracking EC2/ECS resources.
why_misclassified: EC-15 (permission boundary): Role has permission boundary restricting ec2:* and ecs:* to resources tagged with Team=delivery. Payment and core retail resources tagged Team=retail cannot be accessed even though the role policy appears broad.
detection_signal: IAM role retail-delivery-ops-role: ec2:*, ecs:* with Resource: *
ground_truth: Permission boundary policy 'delivery-team-boundary' adds Condition: StringEquals aws:ResourceTag/Team delivery for all EC2 and ECS actions. No access to non-delivery-tagged resources effective.
remediation_impact: Tightening role without understanding permission boundary would disrupt last-mile delivery operations for 3,400 store delivery routes.

scenario: GCP org policy iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation is enabled at org level. CSPM reports org policy compliant. However, retail-vendor-integration project has a project-level override disabling the org policy.
why_misclassified: EC-40 (project override not traversed): CSPM evaluates org policy at organization level and reports compliant. Project-level override that exempts retail-vendor-integration is not detected. SA keys can be created in the excepted project.
detection_signal: Org policy iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation: enforced at organization level. CSPM: compliant.
ground_truth: Project retail-vendor-integration has customConstraint override disabling SA key creation restriction. Override created for vendor onboarding but never removed. SA keys with Editor-level access created post-override.
remediation_impact: Service account keys with Editor access can be created in the excepted project, bypassing org policy intended to prevent key-based credential exposure.

scenario: SAST scan of CodeBuild project retail-security-scanner reports CVE-2024-32002 (git arbitrary code execution, CRITICAL) in the git binary used for SCM checkout. Finding escalated as CRITICAL supply chain risk.
why_misclassified: EC-02 (build layer CVE): git is present in the CodeBuild environment for source checkout only. The vulnerability requires a malicious submodule URL to be cloned. CodeBuild checks out from a trusted private CodeCommit repository with no external submodules.
detection_signal: CodeBuild environment: git 2.44.0 with CVE-2024-32002 (CVSS 9.0) detected
ground_truth: git used exclusively for CodeCommit checkout in a controlled build environment. No external repository URLs or submodules configured. CodeCommit repository is private and write-protected. CVE exploit requires cloning a malicious repo with crafted submodule paths.
remediation_impact: Updating git in build environment image is good practice but CRITICAL escalation overstates urgency given controlled source.

scenario: Macie scans Redshift cluster retail-dw-prod and flags customer_lifetime_value table as containing PII. Table has 18M records with columns: cust_key, age_group, region, ltv_tier, preferred_category.
why_misclassified: EC-20 (empty/non-PII data): cust_key is a surrogate integer key with no mapping to PII data in the data warehouse. age_group is a 10-year bracket. region is a 3-digit postal prefix (not full zip code). LTV and category are computed behavioral metrics — no direct identifiers.
detection_signal: Macie: 18M records with fields matching demographic PII patterns in retail-dw-prod customer_lifetime_value
ground_truth: All direct identifiers stripped in ETL transformation. cust_key has no cross-reference table in DW. age_group and region are coarsened to exceed GDPR k-anonymity threshold (k>5). Reviewed by privacy counsel for GDPR compliance.
remediation_impact: Restricting access to anonymized behavioral metrics halts retail analytics and personalization model development.

scenario: ECS Fargate task definition retail-checkout-task flagged for CVE-2024-24783 (HIGH, Go TLS) in the Fargate platform runtime. Finding requests immediate remediation.
why_misclassified: EC-36 (managed runtime shared responsibility): Fargate platform runtime (including underlying Go TLS libraries used by the Fargate agent) is managed by AWS. Customer code runs in an isolated container above the Fargate platform layer. CVE in Fargate platform runtime is AWS's remediation responsibility.
detection_signal: ECS Fargate task: CVE-2024-24783 in Go TLS runtime component of Fargate platform 1.4.0
ground_truth: CVE is in the Fargate platform agent, not in customer container code. AWS patches Fargate platform transparently. Customer cannot and should not patch Fargate platform components. Shared responsibility: AWS owns platform, customer owns container.
remediation_impact: Customer cannot patch Fargate platform. Ticket generates false urgency for an unremedial finding from the customer perspective.

scenario: GKE node pool retail-prod-nodes shows 4 new nodes with 0% CIS benchmark compliance score. Security team escalates for immediate remediation of new non-compliant nodes.
why_misclassified: EC-23 (warm-up window): Nodes launched 25 minutes ago via cluster autoscaler. GKE Security Posture assessment evaluates nodes on a 30-minute cycle. Nodes not yet assessed — 0% reflects absence of scan data, not actual non-compliance. Nodes provisioned from hardened node image.
detection_signal: GKE node pool: 4 nodes with SecurityPostureScore=0 (not yet evaluated)
ground_truth: Nodes use custom node image with CIS Level 2 baseline pre-applied. GKE Security Posture assessment pending (runs every 30 minutes). Score will populate to 94%+ after first assessment based on prior identical node images.
remediation_impact: Emergency patching newly launched nodes pre-assessment wastes SRE time and may cause service disruption before nodes have processed any traffic.

scenario: Lambda function retail-personalization-v2 has CVE-2024-6387 in its OpenSSH dependency. Feature flag 'personalization-v2-enabled' shows 5% traffic rollout. CSPM suppresses finding since rollout percentage is below 10% threshold.
why_misclassified: EC-45 (partial rollout not suppressed): 5% traffic rollout means the vulnerable function serves 500,000 daily sessions. The below-10% threshold suppression was designed for internal beta features, not customer-facing production traffic. 500K active sessions represents real exposure.
detection_signal: Feature flag personalization-v2-enabled: 5% traffic weight. CSPM: below 10% threshold, suppressed.
ground_truth: 5% of production traffic = 500K daily user sessions touching vulnerable Lambda. CVE-2024-6387 (regreSSHion, CVSS 8.1) in OpenSSH library used for internal SSH connections. Real attack surface active at scale.
remediation_impact: MEDIUM vulnerability active for 500K daily sessions suppressed by percentage threshold not appropriate for production rollouts.

scenario: EKS pod retail-inventory-sidecar running distroless/static:latest flagged for CVE-2024-7006 (NULL ptr deref in libtiff, AV:L/AC:L). Scanner reports HIGH based on CVSS base score.
why_misclassified: EC-29 (distroless image, AV:L unexploitable): CVE-2024-7006 requires local access to trigger via crafted TIFF file. Distroless image has no shell, no package manager, no local file system write capability. The inventory sidecar processes JSON messages — no TIFF handling.
detection_signal: EKS pod: libtiff in distroless image with CVE-2024-7006 CVSS 6.5 HIGH. AV:L attack vector.
ground_truth: AV:L (local access) requires shell access — impossible in distroless. Container processes only JSON inventory data — no TIFF parsing code paths. Vulnerability is architecturally unexploitable.
remediation_impact: Patching libtiff in distroless requires base image rebuild for a library with zero code path reachability in this application.

scenario: SQS queue retail-order-events allows sqs:SendMessage from Principal: * (all principals). Scanner flags HIGH for public SQS queue that could receive unauthorized messages.
why_misclassified: EC-18 (VPC endpoint deny compensates): SQS resource policy appears to allow all, but has aws:sourceVpce condition requiring messages originate from specific VPC endpoint vpce-0sqs-retail. Internet traffic cannot send messages despite the broad Principal.
detection_signal: SQS queue retail-order-events resource policy: Principal=* Action=sqs:SendMessage (no explicit condition shown in summary)
ground_truth: Full policy includes Condition: StringEquals aws:sourceVpce vpce-0sqs-retail. Only resources in the retail VPC with access to the endpoint can send messages. Internet principals blocked by VPC endpoint condition.
remediation_impact: Restricting Principal would require enumeration of all Lambda and EC2 principals that send to queue, creating maintenance burden for auto-scaling workloads.

scenario: Azure Function App retail-reports-legacy has CVE-2024-38094 (HIGH, Microsoft SharePoint) in a .NET dependency. Finding requires emergency patching.
why_misclassified: EC-04 (dead code path): Microsoft.SharePoint.Client library is referenced in the function codebase from a previous integration attempt but the code path is never reached — the SharePoint integration was replaced with direct SharePoint REST API calls 18 months ago. The dead code path loads the library but never calls any SharePoint methods.
detection_signal: Azure Function retail-reports-legacy: CVE-2024-38094 in Microsoft.SharePoint.Client.dll (referenced in project)
ground_truth: SharePoint client library loaded but code path disabled by feature flag SharepointClientEnabled=false in app config. No SharePoint client methods called in function execution. Library effectively dead code.
remediation_impact: Removing dead library reference requires code cleanup but CRITICAL/HIGH urgency overstated for unreachable code.

scenario: GCP IAM key rotation policy flags SA key for retail-inventory-sa as overdue. Key shows creation_time 95 days ago, exceeding 90-day rotation policy.
why_misclassified: EC-25 (immutable rotation): Key was rotated 4 days ago. New key created and deployed. Old key (95 days old) is in a disabled state awaiting deletion after 7-day rollback validation. Scanner sees old disabled key and reports the creation_time without checking key state.
detection_signal: SA key for retail-inventory-sa: key_id=abc123, created 95 days ago. Policy: rotate every 90 days.
ground_truth: Key abc123 is DISABLED (disabled_time: 4 days ago). Active key def456 created 4 days ago. Rotation completed on schedule. Disabled key retained for rollback window per key management policy.
remediation_impact: Re-rotating already-rotated SA disrupts inventory sync service and creates unnecessary key proliferation.

scenario: GCP Security Command Center reports LOW for GCS bucket retail-customer-exports lacking uniform bucket-level access. The LOW rating reflects GCP's baseline severity for bucket policy configuration findings.
why_misclassified: EC-47 (CSP severity non-equivalence): GCP rates this configuration issue as LOW but the bucket contains full customer export data (name, address, purchase history) for GDPR data portability requests. Same finding on AWS Security Hub for S3 would be rated HIGH due to public access concern.
detection_signal: GCP SCC: storage.buckets.uniformBucketLevelAccess=false — LOW severity on retail-customer-exports
ground_truth: Bucket contains GDPR Article 20 customer data exports (full PII). Without uniform access, ACL-based public grants possible. Effective risk is HIGH for GDPR data exposure. GCP's LOW baseline inappropriate for PII-containing buckets.
remediation_impact: LOW SLA allows 90 days for PII exposure risk. GDPR requires protection of data subjects' personal data — 90-day window for remediation is non-compliant with GDPR principle of appropriate security.
